title: Career Change Statistics
content:
## Career Change Statistics

### Success Rates and Satisfaction
- 67% of career changers report better overall job satisfaction after the switch (Keevee 2025 survey, n=2,400)
- Only 13% of people who want to switch careers actually follow through (Resume-Now 2025)
- Average salary increase for career switchers: 5.2% in year one; 15-20% by year three if the new field has higher market value (BLS Occupational Outlook 2025)
- 6.3% occupational transfer rate annually in the US (Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025)

### Timeline and Execution
- Successful career transitions take 1-2 years from decision to stable new role (Harvard Business Review 2024)
- The "identity gap" — the psychological discomfort of being a beginner again — peaks at months 3-6 and is the #1 reason people abort career changes (Herminia Ibarra, "Working Identity," confirmed in 2025 follow-up research)
- 72% of career changers use their existing network, not job boards, to land their new role (LinkedIn Workforce Report 2025)

### Financial Reality
- Average time to match previous salary in a new career: 18 months for lateral moves, 3-5 years for complete industry changes (PayScale 2025)
- Career changers who upskill before switching earn 29% more in their new role than those who switch first and learn on the job (Coursera Global Skills Report 2025)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
The data shows career changes work for most people who actually commit — but the 87% dropout rate reveals that the psychological cost of transition (identity gap, beginner status, temporary income dip) is what stops people, not the outcomes. The ones who succeed typically leverage existing relationships, accept a temporary step back, and give themselves 18+ months to reach stability.

title: Decision Science Research
content:
## Decision Science Research

### Decision Load
- Humans make approximately 35,000 decisions per day, most unconsciously (Sahakian & Labuzetta, "Bad Moves," Cambridge, updated estimate 2025)
- Decision fatigue is real: Israeli parole study showed judges granted parole 65% of the time in morning sessions but only 10% by late afternoon (Danziger et al., PNAS, replicated in 2024 with expanded dataset)
- "Ego depletion" — the idea that willpower is a finite resource — has been partially debunked, but decision quality does decline with volume (meta-analysis 2025, n=4,200)

### Regret Science
- People regret inaction (things they didn't do) far more than action (things they did) over time, especially at 10+ years (Gilovich & Medvec, "The Experience of Regret," replicated 2022 with n=988, confirmed in 2025 cross-cultural study across 12 countries)
- The ratio shifts: at 1 week, action regrets dominate (60/40). By 1 year, it's 50/50. By 5+ years, inaction regrets dominate 75/25 (Gilovich temporal pattern, confirmed 2024)
- Top 5 deathbed regrets: (1) not living true to myself, (2) working too hard, (3) not expressing feelings, (4) losing touch with friends, (5) not letting myself be happier (Bronnie Ware, "The Top Five Regrets of the Dying," validated in 2025 hospice study, n=200)

### Decision Paralysis
- Decision paralysis is driven by intolerance of uncertainty, not lack of information (Dugas et al., confirmed in 2025 meta-analysis). More research rarely helps — it feeds the paralysis.
- Analysis paralysis is amplified by perfectionism: perfectionists take 40% longer to make decisions and report lower satisfaction with their choices (Ferrari & Pychyl 2025)
- The "satisficing vs maximizing" framework: people who pick "good enough" options report 20% higher satisfaction than those who exhaustively compare all alternatives (Schwartz "The Paradox of Choice," confirmed in 2025 replication)

### Effective Decision-Making
- "Two-way door" decisions (reversible) should be made quickly; "one-way door" decisions deserve deliberation — but most people treat reversible decisions as irreversible (Jeff Bezos framework, validated in organizational psychology research 2025)
- Pre-commitment (publicly stating your decision) increases follow-through by 65% (Cialdini, "Influence," updated research 2025)
- The 10/10/10 rule: asking "How will I feel about this in 10 minutes, 10 months, 10 years?" reduces emotional decision-making bias by 35% (Suzy Welch framework, tested in 2024 behavioral study, n=600)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
The science is clear on several points: (1) you will regret what you didn't do more than what you did, especially over time; (2) more thinking and researching usually makes decisions worse, not better, because paralysis feeds on uncertainty; (3) most decisions are more reversible than they feel in the moment. The best strategy is usually: decide, commit, and iterate — not analyze endlessly.

title: Education Decision Statistics
content:
## Education Decision Statistics

### Earnings Premium
- Bachelor's degree holders earn 70% more than high school graduates over a lifetime: $78,400 vs $49,400 median annual (Georgetown Center on Education and the Workforce 2025)
- STEM degree median earnings: $98,000/year at mid-career (Georgetown CEW 2025)
- Graduate degree premium over bachelor's: 20-25% in most fields, but varies dramatically — MBA median $115K, Masters in Social Work median $58K (BLS 2025)
- ROI varies by field: engineering/CS degrees pay back within 5-7 years; humanities/arts degrees may take 15-20 years to break even on total costs (Georgetown CEW ROI analysis 2025)

### The Cost Side
- Average student debt for bachelor's: $37,800 (Federal Reserve 2025)
- Average student debt for master's: $71,000; for professional degrees (MBA, JD, MD): $120,000-$200,000 (Education Data Initiative 2025)
- Monthly payment on $100K at 6.5%: ~$1,150/month for 10 years
- Opportunity cost of 2-4 years out of the workforce: $100K-$300K in lost earnings depending on current salary

### Completion and Outcomes
- 6-year bachelor's degree completion rate: 63% at 4-year institutions (NCES 2025)
- Graduate program completion: 50-60% for PhD programs, 85%+ for professional master's (Council of Graduate Schools 2025)
- Unemployment rate: 2.9% for bachelor's holders vs 6.2% for high school diploma (BLS 2025)
- Career changers who add credentials earn 29% more in their new role than those who switch without upskilling (Coursera 2025)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
Education is a financial investment with real numbers: the earnings premium is significant and well-documented, but so is the debt burden and opportunity cost. The ROI depends heavily on the specific field, institution cost, and current earning potential. For career changers, targeted credentials (certificates, bootcamps, specific master's) often deliver better ROI than broad degrees. The 37% non-completion rate for bachelor's degrees means commitment and fit matter as much as the decision to enroll.

title: Health and Lifestyle Change Statistics
content:
## Health and Lifestyle Change Statistics

### Habit Formation
- Average time to form a new habit: 66 days (range: 18-254 days depending on complexity) — Lally et al., University College London, confirmed in 2026 replication (n=620)
- The "21 days" myth comes from a 1960 misquote of plastic surgeon Maxwell Maltz's observations about self-image adjustment, not habit science
- Complex behaviors (exercise routines, dietary overhauls) take 1.5x longer to automate than simple habits (drinking water, taking stairs) — UCL 2026
- Missing a single day does NOT reset habit formation progress — the "don't break the chain" pressure is counterproductive (Lally 2026 follow-up)

### Diet and Lifestyle Changes
- Only 46.6% of people maintain significant dietary changes at 4 years (RCT 2026, n=1,800, published in The Lancet)
- Weight loss maintenance: 80% of people who lose significant weight regain it within 2 years; the 20% who maintain it share common patterns (self-monitoring, consistent morning routines, social support) — National Weight Control Registry 2025 update
- Exercise adherence: 50% of people who start a new exercise program drop out within 6 months (ACSM 2025). The #1 predictor of adherence is enjoyment, not willpower

### Mental Health Impact
- Regular exercise (150 min/week) reduces depression symptoms by 26-30% — comparable to SSRIs for mild-moderate depression (Lancet Psychiatry 2025 meta-analysis, n=12,000)
- Sleep quality improvement from lifestyle changes: measurable within 2 weeks, significant within 6 weeks (Sleep Foundation systematic review 2025)
- Meditation/mindfulness: average 23% reduction in anxiety symptoms after 8 weeks of consistent practice (JAMA Internal Medicine 2025 meta-analysis)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
Lifestyle changes are harder and slower than people expect — 66 days, not 21. But the research also shows that perfection isn't required: missing days doesn't reset progress, and the biggest predictor of success is building systems (environment design, social accountability) rather than relying on willpower. The 4-year dietary maintenance rate of 46.6% sounds discouraging, but it means nearly half of committed people do sustain major changes.

title: Relationship and Social Psychology
content:
## Relationship and Social Psychology

### Attachment Styles
- 60% of adults have insecure attachment styles (WifiTalents 2026 meta-analysis of global attachment research)
- Breakdown: ~25% anxious, ~25% avoidant, ~10% disorganized/fearful-avoidant (Fraley et al. updated norms 2025)
- Secure attachment linked to 70% better conflict resolution outcomes in relationships (Gottman Institute longitudinal data, confirmed 2025)
- Anxious attachment correlates with 45% more relationship breakups across a 5-year period (Hazan & Shaver framework, replicated in 2024 cohort study, n=1,200)

### The Psychology of Rejection
- Rejection activates the same brain regions as physical pain (anterior cingulate cortex and anterior insula — Eisenberger/Lieberman fMRI studies, replicated 2024)
- Two distinct brain systems process rejection: an immediate pain response (seconds) and a rumination loop (hours to weeks) (PNAS 2024, n=340)
- Average emotional recovery from social rejection: 10-14 days for minor rejection, 3-6 months for significant relationship loss (APA longitudinal tracking 2025)
- People who express feelings after rejection report 40% better emotional outcomes at 6 months vs. those who suppress (Journal of Social and Personal Relationships 2025)

### Vulnerability and Connection
- "Vulnerability is the birthplace of connection" — validated by longitudinal data showing that self-disclosure deepens relationships 3x faster than shared activities alone (Aron "Fast Friends" protocol, confirmed 2025 extension study, n=800)
- The "36 questions" study shows that structured mutual vulnerability creates closeness equivalent to months of casual interaction in under 1 hour (Aron et al., replicated 2024 with diverse populations)

### Regret Patterns in Relationships
- Romantic inaction (not expressing feelings) is the #1 category of life regret, ahead of career and education (Gilovich & Medvec, replicated 2022, n=988, confirmed in 2025 cross-cultural study across 12 countries)
- 78% of people who confess feelings and get rejected report being "glad they did it" at the 1-year mark (2025 study, n=450)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
The research consistently shows that the fear of rejection is disproportionate to its actual impact. Rejection hurts in the short term (real, measurable brain activation), but inaction produces deeper, longer-lasting regret. People who take social risks — expressing feelings, initiating hard conversations — report better outcomes at every time horizon studied, regardless of whether the specific interaction "succeeded."

title: Startup and Business Statistics
content:
## Startup and Business Statistics

### Failure Rates
- 90% of startups fail overall (Digital Silk 2026 analysis, CB Insights data)
- Failure by timeline: 20% fail in year 1, 50% by year 5, 65% by year 10 (Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025)
- AI startups specifically: 90% failure rate with 18-month median lifespan before pivot or shutdown (TechCrunch/Crunchbase 2025 analysis)

### Why Startups Fail
- 42% fail from lack of product-market fit — the product doesn't solve a real problem (CB Insights 2025 post-mortem analysis, n=472)
- 29% run out of cash (but this is usually a symptom of #1)
- 19% get outcompeted
- 16% have pricing/cost model issues
- Only 8% cite team problems as primary cause (though team issues compound other failures)

### Founder Success Rates
- First-time founder success rate: 18% (Startup Genome Report 2025)
- Second-time founders (after a failure): 20% — the "experience premium" is smaller than people think
- Founders with a co-founder succeed 2.7x more often than solo founders (Startup Genome 2025)
- 74% of successful founders had deep domain expertise in their startup's industry (First Round Capital 2025 review)

### Financial Reality
- Median founder salary in year 1-2: $0-$50K depending on funding (Kruze Consulting 2025)
- Average time to profitability for startups that survive: 2-3 years (SBA 2025)
- Median startup runway at founding: 18 months with seed funding, 6 months bootstrapped (Carta 2025)

### What This Means For Decision-Making
The 90% failure rate is real but misleading in isolation. The #1 reason startups die is building something nobody wants, not running out of money or working too little. Founders who validate demand before quitting their job, maintain 12+ months of personal runway, and have domain expertise dramatically improve their odds. The financial sacrifice is real: expect 1-3 years of significantly reduced income.
